title: GPU resilience sprint backlog + ops hypotheses (triage playbook draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sprint/backlog + playbook draft to capture hypotheses and short-term operational controls for transient GPU node instability observed across multiple clusters (Sept–Oct 2026 window). Focus is on a pragmatic on-call triage checklist, short mitigations that reduce blast radius, concrete telemetry gaps, and a prioritized backlog of follow-ups for the resilience sprint.

Topline problem statement (brief):
We have recurring short-lived GPU node failures characterized by: spikes of correctable ECC counts, follow-on kernel oopses or driver hangs, and in some cases NVLink peer reset events. Most failures are transient—nodes recover on reboot or driver reload—but they cause job evictions and downstream application latency/regeneration storms. Root cause is unknown; likely multifactorial (thermal cycling + PSU rail jitter + driver/firmware edge cases).

Pager one-liner (for responders):
"GPU node(s) reporting rapid correctable-ECC accumulation and NVLink peer resets; if >3 active jobs on node, cordon + migrate, collect diagnostics, and escalate to hardware on-call if ECC count > 100 within 30m or kernel oops repeats after reboot."

Quick triage checklist for pager responders (first 20 minutes):
1) Mark node: cordon in k8s and throttle new allocations (kubectl cordon <node>).
2) Snapshot running pods: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>.
3) Check ECC counters: sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,ecc.errors.correctable.volatile --format=csv,noheader,nounits or use our telemetry query: metrics.gpu_ecc_correctable_total{node="<node>"}.
4) Inspect kernel logs (last 2 hours): journalctl -k --since "2 hours ago" | egrep -i "NVRM|GPU|nvlink|kernel panic|oops|IOMMU|aer_rx". Save to /var/tmp/sre-gpu-logs-<node>.log.
5) Check driver state and versions: nvidia-smi -q, lsmod | grep nvidia, modinfo nvidia.
6) Query NVLink events: dmesg | grep -i nvlink or nvidia-smi nvlink -q. Log link-down/link-up events and timestamps.
7) Thermal & power checks: ipmitool sdr elist | egrep -i "temp|fan|volt"; read GPU fan RPM from vendor sensors and compare against expected baseline.
8) Short mitigation: if ECC correctables are rising quickly (>=100 in 30m) or kernel oops present, schedule immediate reboot during low load window; if node is in Dedicated pool, fall back to draining and hardware-oncall.
9) Collect diag bundle: /opt/sre/bin/gpu-diagnostic-collect.sh --node <node> (produces diagnostics.tar.gz). Upload to incident artifacts.
10) Notify hardware and firmware owners with attached diagnostics.

Suggested immediate automated rules (short-term):
- Alert when per-node correctable ECC rate > 5/min sustained for 10m (severity P2).
- Auto-evict and cordon node if uncorrectable ECC count > 0 or if kernel oops triggers restart loop (P1).
- NVLink peer-reset frequency > 3 within 1h => automated scheduling of maintenance and hardware ticket.

Hypotheses / signals matrix (what to test):
H1: Thermal cycling on GPUs (fan curves + datacenter cooling interactions) causes memory retention instabilities that manifest as correctable ECC surges.
  - Signals: correlation between ambient rack inlet temp spikes and ECC rate; fan RPM anomalies preceding ECC.
  - Quick test: run synthetic load (memtest-like) with controlled fan curve profile; compare ECC accumulation.
H2: PSU/regulator jitter during peak power draws causes voltage transients that flip memory bits intermittently (appears as ECC activity then transient driver issues).
  - Signals: correlated chassis PSU alarms, BMC voltage rails bumps, syslog ACPI events.
  - Quick test: schedule controlled power load ramp and watch BMC sdr and ECC counters.
H3: Interaction between specific driver version + GPU microcode and NVLink topology causes peer resets under certain synthetic traffic patterns.
  - Signals: failures concentrate on nodes with driver X.Y.Z or firmware older than F.
  - Quick test: repro in isolated lab with same driver/firmware and synthetic NVLink stress tool.
H4: Memory DIMM/ASIC degradation on a small subset of cards leading to intermittent correctable bursts before eventual uncorrectable failures.
  - Signals: persistent repeat offenders (same GPU IDs) even after reboots, vendor diagnostics flagging DIMMs.
  - Quick test: vendor memtest and board-level diagnostics in lab.

Data & telemetry gaps to fill (short list):
- Per-GPU time-series for correctable vs uncorrectable ECC with 10s granularity (we currently sample at 60s).
- Correlated BMC PSU/rail telemetry surfaced into our SRE metrics platform and joined with GPU metrics.
- NVLink event logs ingested as structured events (current dmesg parsing is ad-hoc).
- Synthetic repro job for NVLink stress and a nightly DIMM memtest scheduled on a small canary fleet.

Immediate backlog and sprint tasks (prioritized):
P0 (must fix now):
- Implement auto-cordon-and-evict rule for nodes with uncorrectable ECC or kernel oops restart loops (owner: eng-sre, issue: SRE-1458).
- Add 10s-granularity ECC ingestion pipeline and a short retention policy for high-resolution windows (owner: infra-metrics).

P1 (next sprint):
- Build and deploy NVLink synthetic stress job + reproduce harness in a lab cluster (owner: applied-ml + eng-sre).
- Wire BMC PSU & rail metrics into SRE metrics and create joint dashboards (owner: infra).
- Create a hardware-ticket template and runbook steps for first-line hardware engineers (owner: platform-engineering).

P2 (later):
- Investigate driver/firmware matrix and plan controlled rollouts of driver update on canary nodes (owner: serving-runtime + release-engineering).
- Policy + cost analysis for replacing persistent offender cards vs keeping them in low-priority pools (owner: procurement + eng-sre).

Runbook draft: node progression decision tree (condensed)
- If uncorrectable ECC => immediate cordon + power-cycle + schedule DOA hardware escalation.
- If correctable ECC spike but no kernel oops => cordon, migrate workloads, monitor for 60m; if counts stop rising, uncordon after verification.
- If NVLink peer reset(s) with no ECC evidence => collect nvlink logs, reduce NVLink-heavy workloads on node, schedule repro.
- If kernel oops / GPU driver panic => force reboot; if panic recurs on boot, hand off to hardware on-call with diag bundle.

Field ticket template (to include in vendor ticket):
- Node hostname / serial / rack position
- Affected GPU PCI IDs and serial numbers
- Timestamped ECC correctable/uncorrectable counts and NVLink peer-reset times
- Attach diagnostic bundle (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q, BMC sdr, ipmitool logs)
- Short reproduction steps observed and whether reboot cleared issue

Acceptance criteria for postmortems (when we declare a fix):
1) Repro within lab or root cause traced to hardware/firmware/driver combination.
2) Reduction of P1/P2 incidents of this class by >= 80% over 30 days post-fix.
3) New telemetry coverage in place (10s ECC + BMC rails) and automated runbook rules live.

Open questions / unresolved items: (for review meeting)
- Are there recurring offenders (card serials) that need warranty replacement? Inventory query needed.
- What is the acceptable operational tolerance for aggressive auto-eviction for Dedicated nodes? (customer implications)
- Do we have capacity to run nightly memtests at scale, or do we need a sampled canary fleet?

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize and ship the auto-cordon/evict rule (eng-sre + infra-metrics) and document implications for Dedicated pools.
- Launch a short lab repro effort for NVLink stress (applied-ml + platform-engineering).
- Schedule a 60-minute review with hardware partners and release-engineering to map driver/firmware matrix and rollout plan (invite list: Priya, Ethan, Marta, Jonah, Alex R., Claire H.).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working draft. Please comment inline on the hypotheses you think we should deprioritize, and add any missing tests you ran during your on-call shifts. We will convert the final runbook to the SRE runbooks repo once stabilized.
